lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: We can't stand it, Pluto. This dog Menippus, living right next door — either move him somewhere else, or we relocate.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What harm is he doing you? He's dead on the same terms as the rest of you.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we're wailing and groaning — Midas here crying over his gold, Sardanapalus over his luxury, and I over my treasuries — he laughs at us. Calls us slaves. Calls us scum. Sometimes he starts singing right over our laments just to ruin them. The man is a complete pest.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Menippus. What do you say to that?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All true. I can't stand them — base, destructive types, the lot of them. Living badly wasn't enough; now they're dead and they're still clinging to the world above. So yes, I enjoy annoying them.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Even so, you shouldn't. They've lost real things.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you losing your mind, Pluto? Siding with their groaning?

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Not at all. I just don't want a war in my jurisdiction.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then, you absolute dregs of Lydia, Phrygia, and Assyria — get this straight: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I follow. I will annoy you, sing at you, and laugh at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. The outrage was what you did — demanding worship, lording it over free men, never once giving death a thought. So now you can wail. You've been stripped of all of it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent. Keep it up — you mourn, I'll sing 'Know thyself' as the refrain. It suits this kind of wailing perfectly.
